selection_reasoning: Mining a polished_granite_slab is a straightforward, observable, and verifiable task. The agent needs to find and break a polished granite slab block in the environment, which results in the item appearing in their inventory. This task doesn't require deep Minecraft domain knowledge — the agent simply needs to locate the block and mine it. It's easily verifiable by checking inventory contents. The scene can be designed with polished granite slabs placed in a visible, accessible location.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining a polished granite slab with a pickaxe causes the item to drop and enter the player's inventory. The player starts with no polished_granite_slab in inventory (only an iron_pickaxe), so having at least 1 confirms successful mining. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks per the design philosophy — it directly reflects the task outcome rather than relying on position or event counters.

scene_description: A cleared 11x11 grass platform with a 2x2 cluster of polished granite slabs placed 3-4 blocks from spawn. The area above is cleared of trees/leaves to ensure visibility. Player is given an iron pickaxe to mine the slabs efficiently. The pinkish slabs contrast well against the green grass for easy visual identification.
task_text: Mine a polished granite slab. Look for the pinkish stone slabs on the grass platform nearby and break one with your pickaxe.
design_notes: The 11x11 grass platform provides a clean, flat surface. Air fill removes any trees/leaves above to ensure clear line of sight. The 2x2 slab cluster at ~3,~0,~3 to ~4,~0,~4 is close enough to spot quickly (~4.2 blocks diagonal from spawn) but far enough to require some movement. Four slabs provide redundancy — only 1 needs to be mined. Iron pickaxe ensures the stone-type block drops as an item (required for stone slabs). No silk touch needed — polished granite slabs drop themselves when mined with any pickaxe.
